newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban threaten hangings if Kabul attacks persist.
newsitem.headline: Taleban threaten hangings if Kabul attacks persist.

text.p: A senior Taleban official has threatened to begin hanging some prisoners if attacks on Kabul, which it has blamed on the opposition alliance, are repeated.

"We have arrested some people on charges of terrorism in the past, and if yesterday's incident is repeated in the future, we will have to hang those who are already in our custody as an example to others." Mullah Khairullah Khairkhwa, the Taleban governor of Kabul province, told journalists on Monday.
An air-raid on Sunday hit Kabul's northeastern residential suburb of Wazir Akbar Khan killing four people and wounding 15.
The attack destroyed three houses, including the office of the United Nations World Health Organisation, and collapsed part of the perimeter wall of the nearby United States embassy.
The mullah said the air raid had been carried out by jets belonging to opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum in revenge for losses he sustained on the front line north of Kabul ten days ago.

"It was a deliberate and indiscriminate act by Dostum as a result of his defeat in Qarabagh (some 40 kilometers, 25 miles north of Kabul). The opposition coalition have completely failed in launching any successful attack against the Taleban and because of their failure they target residential areas."

After a lull of more than a month, there have been several air raids on Kabul since December 28, when the fundamentalist Taleban launched an offensive north of Kabul forcing back the opposition 10 km (six miles),
The mullah also accused the opposition of carrying out a bombing in a crowded vegetable market in the capital on Sunday.
Four people are said to have died in the blast, and local traders in the market said on Monday that 37 were wounded. Local hospitals said they had admitted 25 people from the explosion.
"In order to show that the joint opposition can disrupt the Taleban administration in Kabul, they killed many civilians without thinking of the price." he told journalists.
There have been no claims of responsibility and no comment from the opposition alliance of forces loyal to the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani and their ally Dostum.

The mullah said that despite Sunday's incidents, the Taleban were still willing to allow the International Committee of the Red Cross to transport the bodies of dead opposition fighters across the front line as a gesture of goodwill.
When the Taleban took the villages of Qarabagh, Qaloqan and Istalif on December 28, a number of bodies of opposition fighters were left in territory captured by the Taleban.

"Eighty bodies of the enemy from fighting in Qarabagh, Qaloqan and Istalif will be returned to the other side tomorrow in a Red Cross convoy as a gesture of goodwill by the Taleban and to show that we also abide by international and humanitarian rules." he said.
He said the reason for the delay in returning the bodies was that the front line had been too active since the offensive.
The Taleban captured Kabul in September and now control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan. They are enforcing a strict Islamic code.
